reason: Only D complies with the request; A ignores it, B reverses the direction the line asks for (bring it UP FROM the dock), C answers as the requester.
A survives because the line says the device is fixed and says nothing about when it must be collected, so arranging a later pickup is a perfectly cooperative reply alongside B.
The line is an alternative question and only B answers it; A, C and D reply to offers or complaints that were never made.
Only C takes up the offer; A treats an offer as a settled ruling, B substitutes a written procedure for the offered meeting, D puts the mediation in the past.
Only A accepts being kept on Friday; B answers about Sundays, C contradicts 'you're still on', D negotiates a partial release the line has already refused.
Only A answers the which-door question; B, C and D reply to a request, a loss decision and a recovery that the line never raises.
Only C answers the yes/no experience question; B fetches equipment, D responds to an ongoing emergency, A to a booking.
Only C responds to a used copy being available now; A orders one anyway, D talks about buying new, B answers an unasked question about the course.
Only B answers the proposed split; C takes on the cartons the speaker claimed, A replies to a delivery check, D leaves the proposal unanswered.
Only A does something with the room-number rule; B signs for a package not mentioned, C abandons a parcel the line implies is there, D replies to a notification offer.
The offer names the roommate specifically; only C acts on it, B redirects it to other people, A and D reply to unrelated matters.

C survives because nothing in the line rules out an existing Thursday-morning commitment, and 'I'd better move my seminar cover, then' is an ordinary implicit acceptance; A is preferred only for being the more explicit yes.
Only B works around a fully booked counselor; C and D assume an appointment the line rules out, A answers a question that was not asked.
Only A acts on being redirected to the welfare office; B, C and D respond to rights, printing and a document fix that the line never mentions.
The word 'instead' presupposes the hearer would otherwise return the trolley, so A's relief at not having to bring it back is fully supported by the line and competes with D's plain compliance.
Only C answers the request to be out; B and D redirect to clearing shelves and cupboards without answering, A reacts to good news the line does not give.
Only A agrees to take the reading; B replies to a visit announcement, C to reassurance, D asks for a figure the speaker has just asked the hearer to supply.
Only D responds to the instalment offer; A's and B's 'that'/'just before' have no antecedent in the line, and C signs something never mentioned.

B survives on the same reasoning as C — one semester leaves the other half to fill, whether by keeping the courses already timetabled or by looking at what is still open — and the line says nothing that favours either.
Only B answers the how-short question; C puts the cut in the past, D gives a yes to a wh-question, A replies to a wait.
Only C deals with having no cash; A and B carry on ordering as if the line had not been said, D replies to a forgotten item.
The line never says what about the weekends changed, so C's rescheduling of weekend practice fits the same tacit reading as B's watching Saturday evenings; the item is underspecified.
Only D engages the fire-door failure; C's 'that's ours' has no referent, A replies to a re-inspection date and B to a shelving question.
A survives because the line only presupposes (never states) that the hearer holds the key, and correcting that presupposition — the dance group took it Tuesday — is an ordinary reply to the request.

B survives as a plain consequence of the ridge being dropped for a walking party that had planned an overnight on it; the line neither states nor rules out that plan, so it is no more of a supplement than D's valley loop.
Only A answers the now-or-keeping alternative; B answers quantity, D changes the item, C accepts an offer never made.
Only B works around having no card today; C collects a card the line says does not exist, A accepts an unmade offer, D's dining office does not follow from a printer fault.

The porters' agreement leaves the timing open, so C's 'after dinner?' is a normal next move; only the conditional shade of 'that'd make it easier' favours A, which is a naturalness preference rather than a refutation.
Only A addresses the shortfall; C treats a cut award as more money, D waits for a decision already made, B sends an item the line never mentions.
Only A reacts to a waived charge; B still supplies evidence, C still waits for the outcome, D pays a fine the line cancelled.
Only A accepts the solo; B and C both treat the hearer as not playing it, D replies to a correction rather than an assignment.
Only B undertakes to capture the error message; A, C and D respond to a broken machine or a writing task the line never raises.
Only A collects the ready refill; C chooses a formulation already dispensed, B and D treat the prescription as unfilled or out of stock.
Only D responds to a defeat; B proceeds as if it passed, C writes a proposal already voted on, A reacts to relief the line does not offer.
Only D uses the earlier Friday opening; A and C read the change as evening time gained or an hour lost, B abandons the lab entirely.
Only A acts on a change of venue; B, C and D respond to a records question, a project phase and a change of scope that the line does not announce.
Only C follows from a repaired fridge; D still waits for a part, B schedules a visit already made, A draws a causal link the line does not support.
Only C takes the finished poster away; B and D re-edit a job the line says is done and looks good, A answers an unasked packaging question.
Only A acts on where participants now get credit; B, C and D address room booking, recruitment and consent forms, none of which the line touches.
Only D responds to losing the shift; A accepts an alternative shift the line never offers, B and C carry on with the work as if nothing was cut.
Only B seeks an alternative; C waits for a service the line says is discontinued, D waits for the shuttle anyway, A books something never mentioned.
Only A addresses the arrears; B answers an unasked name question, D accepts an unmade tariff offer, C's wrong-company conclusion has no basis in the line.
Only C responds to appeals against the hearer's own marking; A's 'his' has no referent among plural students, B accepts unoffered help, D disclaims the section the line assigns.
Only C relocates for the night; B returns tonight despite 'nobody tonight', A's 'that one' has no referent, D reacts as if the news helped.
